description: How RailMon spells the host of a destination: each case is an authority (a Host header or :authority, or the host and port of a URL) and the host RailMon writes for it in declared_destinations, observed_destinations and undeclared_destinations. The host is in lower case, without its port, without an IPv6 address's brackets, and without one trailing dot. A reader that records calls to a destination, such as railguard's proxy, spells a host this way too, so its records and RailMon's bundle name one host alike. Only authorities every reader accepts are here; what a reader does with a malformed one (an empty or non-numeric port, a user part, a character no host name has) is its own.
readers: src/observed.rs normalize_host, run by its tests
